brand.note: Locked by the user. Used as a fully dipped field on money screens, not as an accent stroke. User-selectable across nine hues at runtime; every derivation below is recomputed by applyThemeColor().

brand-text.note: The brand when it is text or icon on ground rather than a field. Raised in dark mode (7.2:1 on dark surface) because the field-strength blue is unreadable as text there.

brand-dim.note: Secondary text ON the dipped field. Tinted from the brand's own hue, never grey. Computed as hue + max(sat+16,60)% + 90% L so it clears 4.5:1 at any of the nine accents.

brand-press.note: Pressed state of any brand-filled control. Computed as L − 8.

brand-deep.note: Shadow color under brand-filled elements. Computed as L − 22, sat + 3.

ink-faint.note: Third tier for genuinely secondary meta. Set at 46% not 48% because at 48% the ratio is 4.28:1 on ground — passing on a card but failing on the page behind it, and this meta appears on both. 4.60:1 on ground.

hairline.note: In dark mode this is the sole separation mechanism; in light mode surfaces use the shadow instead.

display.purpose: The hero amount on a dipped screen panel. One per screen, tabular, weight 800.

headline.purpose: The screen's single lead metric — dipped card amount, report total.

title.purpose: Screen-entry titles on standalone surfaces (login, auth, onboarding).

heading.purpose: Page header title, dialog and section titles.

body-sm.purpose: Chip and segment labels, dense list meta, panel labels.

amount.purpose: Running total inside the action button; inline money in lists.

label.purpose: Nav labels, service tile labels, header subtitles.

label-micro.purpose: Uppercase column label for a stat row (MASUK / KELUAR / KASBON) and small counters. Never a kicker above a heading.

fonts.purpose: Offline-first: the app runs in warungs with no signal, so a remote font would make the app's voice depend on the network its own scenario lacks. Declared to 800 because every money object is set at 800 and an undeclared weight gets browser-synthesized into a bloated fake bold.
Reserved for places that genuinely need a monospace.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The one elevation level. Light theme only; in dark theme surfaces separate with a border and shadow-none. Every legacy alias (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, card, card-lg, soft, soft-lg, soft-xl, elevated) maps to this exact value on purpose.

shadows.name: lift-brand
shadows.purpose: Depth under brand-filled elements — action button, primary button, dipped money card, raised cashier nav button. Built from --primary-deep so it stays correct at any of the nine accents. Aliased as shadow-primary / glow / glow-lg.

shadows.name: lift-destructive
shadows.purpose: The same treatment under a destructive fill.

motion.name: amount-land
motion.value: amount-land 0.42s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; from { transform: translateY(0.22em) scale(0.97) } to { transform: translateY(0) scale(1) }
motion.purpose: The app's only authored beat: a money value landing when it changes. Starts from an already-visible state (opacity is never animated) so the number cannot disappear if the animation does not run, and touches transform only — no layout, no blur, nothing paid per frame on a low-end Android WebView.

motion.name: press
motion.value: transform 100ms; active: scale(0.985) on the action button, scale(0.98) on buttons
motion.purpose: Touch feedback. A state transition, not an authored beat.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global flattening; components additionally carry motion-reduce: variants.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.note: Page gutters 16px → 32px; tile grid 4 → 6 columns; product grid 3 → 4.

focus.purpose: One focus language across every interactive element; the outline fallback exists so Chromium never draws its own blue ring inside this palette.

identifierSystem.primary: toneForId(rowId) — ((|id| - 1) % 6) + 1. Sequential Dexie ids guarantee the first six categories get six distinct tones.
identifierSystem.fixed: ROUTE_TONE maps fixed destinations (routes, note types) to a tone so it is never guessed at the call site.
identifierSystem.fallback: toneForName(name) — djb2-style hash mixed with string length and bit-rotated. Documented fallback for records that have nothing but a name; name hashing collapsed the real product grid to one hue.
identifierSystem.ceiling: A seventh category repeats a tone. Deliberate and recorded: repeating beats adding hues until nothing is recognizable.

chrome.safeArea: --app-safe-top / --app-safe-bottom declared once on html and applied there as padding. Components must not re-apply safe-area insets.
chrome.rootFontSize: clamp(0.9375rem, 0.25rem + 3vw, 1.125rem) — ~15.25px on a phone, 18px on a tablet; the whole rem ramp, icons included, grows with it.
chrome.browserSurfaces: Selection, caret, accent-color, and scrollbars are themed from the token set so the parts the browser draws do not fall outside the system (the app also ships inside Electron on Windows, where desktop scrollbars are genuinely visible).

narrative.overview:
Two grammars, one system. Screens whose job is money — kasir, pembayaran, laporan, kasbon, pengeluaran — speak the wallet grammar: the brand color arrives as a fully dipped field at the top of the screen, the amount is the screen's object rather than a caption beside a label, and a thick full-width action row waits at the thumb line above the nav. Screens whose job is choosing — beranda, menu, stok, pengaturan — speak the tile grammar: a grid of colored service tiles where the color is not decoration but an identifier system, one concern holding one color everywhere it appears.

What binds them into one app rather than two is deliberately small: one radius scale, one typeface, and one elevation level. Density is consumer-app density, not desktop-dashboard density: 44-54px touch targets, 16px page gutters, 8px as the default gap. The craft bar is the Indonesian consumer super-app (Gojek/GoPay) — their grammar was taken, never their brand colors. Brand blue hsl(227 57% 48%) (#3554C1) is a locked user constraint.

The build serves a warung owner on a low-end Android phone, one-handed, often in direct sunlight, often offline. That is why the display face is self-hosted rather than fetched, why there is exactly one authored motion beat, and why nothing in app chrome pays a per-frame cost. Confirmed rejection: the uniform neutral shadcn card grid where every screen looks the same and no single object leads.
keyCharacteristics: Brand color as a dipped field, not an accent stroke
Money set tabular, extra-bold (800), with negative tracking
Six-color category identifier system, reused across tiles, chips, thumbnails, and lists
One elevation level; one separation mechanism per theme
Drawn (Lucide) icons only, never emoji, never glyph characters
Flat fields: no gradients, no glass, no stacked shadows

rules.name: The Dipped Field Rule
rules.body: On money screens the brand is a field, not an accent. One dipped panel per screen — never two. Secondary text on that field uses Brand Haze, tinted from the brand's own hue; grey on blue reads dirty and drops below 4.5:1 at every accent option.

rules.name: The Unlit Dark Field Rule
rules.body: The brand field is not lightened in dark mode. Lightening it drops white-on-brand from 6.6:1 to 4.9:1. The locked blue is used as-is; only its text derivation is raised.

rules.name: The Three Roles Rule
rules.body: A category tone is never used as a single value. Solid fill, tint surface, and ink-on-tint are three separate tokens, and ink on a tint is always the -on value — never the solid.

rules.name: The Row-ID Tone Rule
rules.body: A category's tone comes from its row id (toneForId), not from hashing its name. Name hashing collapsed the real product grid to one hue — 'Makanan' and 'Minuman' landed on the same color and the identifier system died exactly where it was needed. toneForName is a documented fallback for records that have nothing but a name. Fixed destinations (routes, note types) are listed in ROUTE_TONE, never guessed at the call site.

rules.name: The Six-Tone Ceiling
rules.body: Six tones means a seventh category repeats a color. That limit is deliberate and recorded: repeating beats adding hues until nothing is recognizable.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every number that represents money is tabular-nums and never lighter than 600. MoneyDisplay and MoneyPanelAmount own the ramp; th/td inherit tabular figures globally so columns of numbers line up.

rules.name: The Rp Rule
rules.body: The currency prefix is dimmed by size and weight (0.8em, 600), never by opacity — opacity mixes it with whatever is behind it, and these amounts stand on a dipped brand field.

rules.name: The Micro Label Rule
rules.body: The uppercase tracked micro label is a column label for numbers. It is not a kicker or an eyebrow: never place it above a heading to announce a category.

rules.name: The One Mechanism Rule
rules.body: One separation mechanism per theme. Light: shadow, border-transparent. Dark: border-border, shadow-none. A surface that ships both is a defect, not a variant.

rules.name: The No-Chrome-Blur Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-blur in app chrome. The page header and the bottom nav sit on solid surfaces because blur costs a frame on every scroll in a low-end Android WebView and cuts contrast in sunlight. (Modal, dialog, and sheet scrims do use a 2px blur — that is a one-shot overlay, not scrolling chrome, and it is part of the shipped world.)

rules.name: The Inside Badge Rule
rules.body: Badges sit inside their container, never hung outside it. Outer badges get clipped by scroll containers and by the page's own padding edge.

rules.name: The One Beat Rule
rules.body: The app has exactly one authored motion beat: amount-land (translateY(0.22em) scale(0.97) to rest, 420ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), fired when a money value changes. It starts from a state that is already visible — opacity is never animated — so the number cannot disappear if the animation does not run, and it touches transform only. Everything else is a state transition (colors, a 0.98 press scale), and prefers-reduced-motion flattens all of it globally.

dos: Do pick the grammar by the screen's job: money screens get a dipped panel plus an action bar; choosing screens get the tile grid.
Do derive a category's tone from its row id via toneForId, and register fixed destinations in ROUTE_TONE.
Do use all three tone roles correctly: solid for marks, -bg for the surface, -on for anything drawn on that surface.
Do use Brand Haze ({colors.brand-dim}) for secondary text on a dipped field, never a grey.
Do separate a surface one way only: shadow in light, border in dark.
Do set every money number tabular, at 600 or heavier.
Do add any new brand derivation to applyThemeColor, so it survives all nine user-selectable accents.
Do keep badges and counters inside their container's bounds.
Do give interactive elements the standard 3px focus ring and a 44px minimum touch target.
donts: Don't lighten the brand field in dark mode — it lowers white-on-brand contrast from 6.6:1 to 4.9:1. Raise the text derivation instead.
Don't put a border and a shadow on the same surface.
Don't ship more than one dipped money panel or more than one action bar per screen.
Don't use backdrop-blur on scrolling app chrome (headers, nav, bars).
Don't use gradients, glass fills, or stacked/multi-level shadows — there is one elevation.
Don't hard-code a brand derivative as a literal HSL in CSS.
Don't hash a category name for its color when a row id exists.
Don't add a seventh category hue; repeating a tone is the recorded trade.
Don't use emoji or text glyphs as icons — icons are drawn (Lucide) at 18px or 22px.
Don't animate anything beyond the one amount-land beat and ordinary state transitions.
Don't hang a badge outside its container, and don't add safe-area padding in a component — the root already applied it.
Don't use the uppercase micro label as a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
